activities.title: Student Introduction and Study-Time Card guided Build

contract.doing: Create a plain IntelliJ Java project named `student-introduction`. In `Main.java`, print a learner name, course, planned weekly minutes, and calculated hours/remainder from supplied values. Run the same saved class from IntelliJ and PowerShell, then deliberately reproduce and repair one missing-semicolon compile error and one zero-divisor runtime error using the first useful diagnostic.
contract.why: Every later practical depends on knowing which source class ran, whether it compiled, and how to repair one reported cause instead of guessing.
contract.output: A `student-introduction` project with Main.java and evidence.md proving two run routes and two evidence-led repairs.
contract.tools: Windows, a current supported JDK, IntelliJ IDEA, and PowerShell
contract.prerequisites: Only verified setup capabilities and this Week's Core Study are required.
contract.finished: The intended saved Main.java runs from IntelliJ and the documented PowerShell command. 95 minutes produces 1 hour and 35 minutes in labelled output. The compile record names the diagnostic and repaired source line. The runtime record names ArithmeticException, the application line, and the repaired divisor. No input, branches, loops, or calculator interface are introduced yet.
contract.submission: Project/JDK identity plus IntelliJ and PowerShell run commands | Final labelled 95-minute output | Missing-semicolon compiler diagnostic and repair | ArithmeticException stack-frame evidence and repair

steps: Create the project with the verified JDK and IntelliJ build system, create `src/Main.java`, paste the starter, save, and run it once from the gutter.
Replace the starter values with a learner name, course, and `int minutes = 95`; calculate hours with `/ 60` and remaining minutes with `% 60`, then print four labelled lines.
Open IntelliJ Terminal in the project, compile to `out` with the supplied command, run the class, and record how source, compiler output, class output, and JVM execution differ.
Delete one semicolon, rebuild, record the first compiler message and location, repair only that line, and rerun.

Create `evidence.md` with both commands, expected/actual output, the two diagnostics, cause, one-line repair, and final clean rerun.

activities.title: Campus Profile Collector guided Build

contract.doing: Build a console profile collector using one Scanner and `nextLine()` for every prompt: name, programme, level, age text, and commuter yes/no. Parse age with `Integer.parseInt`, normalize the commuter answer, and print an exact summary. In a disposable comparison block, create two equal-content Strings and prove why `.equals` is the decision operation.
contract.why: Introductory practicals repeatedly combine typed values, console input, conversion, and exact String decisions; one stable input pattern prevents confusing newline bugs.
contract.output: A Campus Profile Collector with predictable Scanner use, typed values, four valid cases, one recorded invalid conversion, and correct String comparison.
contract.tools: Windows, a current supported JDK, IntelliJ IDEA, and PowerShell
contract.prerequisites: Previously completed competencies: JAVA-C001, JAVA-C002, JAVA-C003. New Week concepts are taught in Core Study before this Build.
contract.finished: All five prompts accept the supplied cases without a skipped field. Age is stored as int only after parsing and the invalid-age exception is recorded. Commuter decisions use equals or equalsIgnoreCase rather than ==. The output labels and boolean result match all four valid cases. The String demonstration explains content versus reference comparison in the learner’s own words.
contract.submission: Five-prompt transcript with a spaced name | Four-case expected-versus-actual table | Invalid-age exception evidence | == versus equals output and corrected decision line

activities.title: Persistent Study Notes guided Build

contract.doing: Persist records as `id|topic|text` UTF-8 lines in `data/notes.txt`. IDs start at 1 and use highest loaded ID plus 1. A missing file means first run; any non-three-part line or nonnumeric ID is malformed and stops the load without writing. Implement add/list/topic filtering and a `Checks.java` harness with six named cases.
contract.why: A dependable program must preserve learner data, make failure types visible, and provide a repeatable way to prove repairs.
contract.output: A persistent notes tool with six passing dependency-free checks, restart evidence, malformed-data preservation, and one debugger-led repair.
